newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bonds ended a slow day firmer but traders said there had been a lot of uncertainty in the market and a lack of direction as players awaited the release of money supply figures after the official close.

"There was a lot of nervousness in the market...first it broke more positive as the U.S. appeared to stabilise but in the afternoon it turned around again as the rand ticked weaker," a senior trader said.
At 1400 GMT government's R150 bond was at 15.18 percent from 15.26 percent overnight as all attention was focused on the M3 and private sector credit extension data out at 1500 GMT.
The M3 consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters came in at 15.1 percent from a preliminary January figure of 16.89 percent.
Annual credit growth was seen easing to between 15.50 percent and 16.92 with the consensus at 16.39 percent compared with a preliminary rise of 17.07 percent in January.
"Technically we started the day neutral but there was no clear direction and the current nervousness is on the back of the U.S., the slightly softer rand and the economic data," the trader added.
Others agreed, saying the main direction for Thursday would be determined by the money supply figures.
Foreigners were net sellers of 330.69 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 203.72 million rand's worth on Thursday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes on Thursday were pegged at 7.19 billion rand on Tuesday from 37.82 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date ahead of the long Easter break.

It was also an uneventful day on the local currency market as the rand held to a tight range during the day but ticked slightly weaker in the last hour of official trade as an import order moved through the market.
"Quiet...slow...that's how I would describe the day," a senior forex trader said.
After the drift upward to above the 4.42 level the rand remained stuck, waiting for the M3 data, he added.
At 1400 the currency was at 4.4210/4240 against the U.S. dollar from 4.4175/4205 late on Tuesday.
Some dealers predicted a 4.40 to 4.45 range for the remainder of the week, saying it appeared unlikely the unit would breach the 4.40 level soon after a fleeting attempt on Tuesday.
In the longer term, the expected payment from the Telkom privatisation deal should favour the rand, one said, predicting a test of 4.35 over the next two to three months.
Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.2707/2800 against sterling from 7.2710/2804 and at 0.3777/3782 marks from 0.3769/3773 marks.

Short-term money market rates were quoted slightly higher with three-month deposit rates all at 16.55 percent offered from 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered previously, while the 90-day BA rate was steady at between 15.90 to 16.10 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage dipped slightly to 10.414 billion rand on Tuesday from 10.455 billion rand on Saturday, the Reserve Bank said.
